topic: Addition & Subtraction -- "Column subtraction/addition of numbers with more than 4 digits" (Y5), "Add and subtract integers" (Y6)
lesson_id: cache_key v19|y5m-add-subtract|curriculum|secure|lesson|column subtraction of numbers with more than 4 digits; v19|y5m-add-subtract|...|guided|...; v19|y6m-add-subtract|curriculum|secure|guided|add and subtract integers

steps_to_reproduce: 1. POST http://localhost:3000/api/ks2-lesson with topicId=y5m-add-subtract, skill="Column subtraction of numbers with more than 4 digits", kind=lesson (or guided), force=true. 2. Read response.lesson.workedExample: question="$62,403 - 27,568$", answer="376", steps=["Set up the columns: Write 403 on top and 27 underneath to subtract.", ...], whiteboard.blocks contains a column_method block with rows ["403","-27","376"]. 3. Independently confirmed root cause: `npx tsx -e "import {buildMethodForQuestion} from './lib/methods'; console.log(buildMethodForQuestion('$62,403 - 27,568$'))"` returns builderId=column_subtraction, answer=376 -- byte-identical to the API's output, proving the deterministic builder (not the LLM) authored the wrong answer/steps/whiteboard. 4. Confirmed this happens at serve time, not just at original generation: app/api/ks2-lesson/route.ts:555-559 (inside hardenWorkedExample, called on every cache read at line 848-850) unconditionally overwrites lesson.workedExample.answer with deterministicMathsAnswer(question).answer whenever it disagrees with the model's own answer, treating the deterministic builder as ground truth. 5. Root cause of the builder's wrong answer: lib/methods/normalize-math-text.ts normalizeMathText() never strips thousands-comma separators; lib/methods/column-addition.ts parseSubtractionOperands()/parseAdditionOperands() use regex /(\d{1,6})\s*-\s*(\d{1,6})/ which only matches contiguous digit runs, so on "62,403 - 27,568" it matches the digit run immediately before " - " ("403") and the digit run immediately after ("27"), silently computing 403-27=376 instead of 62403-27568. The same unguarded \d{1,6} pattern (with no comma-stripping) exists in parseMultiplicationOperands (lib/methods/column-multiplication.ts:485-497) and the division operand parser (lib/methods/long-division.ts:224), so any comma-formatted operand >=1,000 in those question types is equally at risk, though not separately reproduced here. 6. Quantified against the live cache (437-row ks2_lesson_cache table, question/answer TEXT fields only -- no pupil data queried): of 30 cached questions matching a pure "A + B" / "A - B" pattern with at least one operand >=1,000, 4 have a stored answer that disagrees with the correct comma-aware arithmetic -- and all 4 are specifically the workedExample field (the main taught example) on the y5m-add-subtract and y6m-add-subtract lessons; every sibling tryThis/guidedPractice/independentPractice/quickCheck question on the SAME lessons, for the SAME skill, is correct. This confirms the defect is isolated to the workedExample-specific override path (route.ts:555-559), not the general answer pipeline (lib/ks2-maths-accuracy.ts's hardenKS2MathsPracticeAnswers, which already correctly excludes workedExample from its own scope and handles the other fields correctly via a different, unaffected code path).
expected_result: The worked example teaching a Year 5/6 pupil column subtraction/addition of 5-digit numbers shows the real question's numbers, correct step-by-step working, a whiteboard matching those numbers, and the correct final answer (e.g. 62,403 - 27,568 = 34,835).
actual_result: The worked example's steps, whiteboard column-method block, and final answer all silently solve a different, much simpler problem (403-27=376) than the question actually displayed above them (62,403-27,568), with no error, warning, or validation failure surfaced anywhere in the API response. This is the exact defect pattern the audit brief calls out by name: "narration to mention content absent from the board" / an architecture where a component's output is disconnected from the authored question. It is currently live in the cache serving real requests (confirmed via a direct, uncached force=true regeneration producing the identical wrong 376 answer, not a stale one-off).
evidence: app/api/ks2-lesson/route.ts:548-559 (hardenWorkedExample override) and :848-850 (applied on cache read); lib/methods/normalize-math-text.ts (full file -- no comma-stripping anywhere); lib/methods/column-addition.ts:240-249 (parseSubtractionOperands regex); lib/methods/column-multiplication.ts:485-497 and lib/methods/long-division.ts:224 (same unguarded pattern, not separately reproduced); raw API response captured via curl (POST /api/ks2-lesson, topicId=y5m-add-subtract, kind=lesson) showing question/steps/whiteboard/answer mismatch; direct call to buildMethodForQuestion() reproducing the identical 376 answer outside the API, isolating the bug to the deterministic builder; live cache sweep (ks2_lesson_cache, 437 rows, question/answer text only) quantifying 4-of-30 pure-calculation comma-formatted questions wrong, all 4 in the workedExample field specifically.
likely_root_cause: normalizeMathText() (shared by every operand parser in lib/methods/) does not strip thousands-comma separators before regex matching; the \d{1,6} operand-matching regexes therefore only see contiguous digit runs and silently truncate any comma-grouped number, producing a confidently wrong but well-formed answer with no exception thrown. app/api/ks2-lesson/route.ts then trusts this deterministic result unconditionally as "single source of truth" (its own comment, line 549-551) and overwrites the LLM's answer -- which in the observed case (tryThis: 73,205-38,467=34,738, correct) was right -- with the parser's wrong one, specifically for the workedExample field.
recommended_fix: Add comma-stripping to normalizeMathText() (e.g. strip a comma between two digits when followed by exactly 3 more digits: /(\d),(?=\d{3}\b)/g -> ''), which is the single shared entry point for every operand parser in lib/methods/ -- this fixes column addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division parsing in one place. No data migration or cache purge is needed: hardenWorkedExample() re-derives the answer on every serve (route.ts:848-850), so the fix self-heals all 437 cached rows the next time each is read. After deploying the fix, re-run the cache sweep to confirm 0-of-N wrong, and specifically re-check the 4 identified rows (cache_key values in steps_to_reproduce).
regression_test: Unit test: parseSubtractionOperands('$62,403 - 27,568$') must return {a:62403,b:27568} (and equivalent tests for +, x, and division parsers with comma-formatted operands >=1,000). Add an integration test asserting POST /api/ks2-lesson for y5m-add-subtract and y6m-add-subtract returns a workedExample.answer matching independently-computed arithmetic on the stated question, for both kind=lesson and kind=guided.
estimated_effort: Small (single shared-function fix + cache self-heals) -- Small to Medium if the multiplication/division parsers need separate confirmation and tests
status: FIXED — normalizeMathText() now strips thousands-comma separators; verified against live cache (4/4 previously-wrong rows self-healed with no purge) and a fresh forced regeneration. Regression tests added in __tests__/lib/normalize-math-text.test.ts. Note: root-cause line corrected during the fix — the actual override is lib/methods/apply-builder.ts:437-441 (applyBuiltToExample), not app/api/ks2-lesson/route.ts:555-559 as originally reported; that second check is a redundant no-op for column ops.
